reasons.dead|aside.atlas-layers: The layer rail is a floating panel ON the map, not a column beside it. It is short on purpose — a rail as tall as the map would cover the city — so the space under it is the map itself. Check it: open /atlas and look under the rail; what is there is satellite imagery and 3D blocks, not an empty band.
reasons.dead|div.atlas-page-tools: The row of page-level doors (city watch, Research & method, Data and sources) floats over the map's top-right corner so the map keeps every pixel of its height. The space under the row is the map. Check it: open /atlas and look under the row; what is there is the city, not an empty band.
reasons.wrap|div.atlas-page-tools: Below 340px the three page-level doors (city watch, Research & method, Data & sources) cannot sit on one row beside the Layers button: they need about 355px at the tightest padding that keeps them legible, and a 320px phone has 320. They wrap, and Data & sources ends up alone on the second row, right-aligned under the others. The alternative is the one that shipped until 22 October 2026: the row ran under Layers and hid its "+". A second short row over the map costs a few lines of city; a button covered by its neighbour costs a door. Check it: open /atlas at 320px wide and see City watch and Research & method on one row, Data & sources below them, and Layers uncovered. Wider than 340px the row is single and this reason does not apply.
